A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D Half-Gaussian Splatting work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3D-HGS and Scaffold-HGS reconstruction results, kernel comparisons, learning-rate sensitivity and training-strategy experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original results for four Half-Gaussian integrations, including image quality, rendering speed, storage requirements and diagnostic experiments.

M1.justification: The paired Half-Gaussian representation remains, but v3 introduces separate opacity-dependent bounds and tile selection for each half, replacing v1's use of standard splatting apart from kernel substitution (Section 3.4; Appendix B.1, Algorithm 1). The projected kernel also changes to incorporate conditional Gaussian mean and variance.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven Mip-NeRF360, two Tanks&Temples and two Deep Blending scenes. v3 adds synthetic one-dimensional square-function fitting in Figure 2, a limited additional task beyond scene rendering.

E2.justification: v3 adds Mip-Splatting and GS-MCMC to the main benchmark comparison; neither participates there in v1. Conversely, the per-scene comparison drops Mip-NeRF and Scaffold-GS, retaining 3D-GS alongside the proposed variants (v1 Tables 5–6 versus v3 Table 5). The separate reconstruction-kernel comparison retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 expands evaluation from image-quality metrics to rendering FPS and storage memory, and adds synthetic fitting. Appendix B.2 explicitly reports modified opacity thresholds for pruning and resetting, 0.01 and 0.02, while the new HGS-MCMC experiment specifies a 0.015 Playroom relocation threshold. These are reported protocol additions or revisions; the retained scene coverage and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's normal-learning-rate sensitivity study and four-way training-strategy ablation disappear (Figure 6 and Table 4). v3 adds square-function approximation, learned-opacity distributions and Bonsai grayscale-profile analyses (Figures 2, 5 and 9). The reconstruction-kernel ablation and depth/normal comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or performance uncertainty. The new opacity histograms characterize learned parameters rather than uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: Many retained scores change: 3D-HGS Mip-NeRF360/Tanks&Temples PSNR changes from 29.56/24.49 to 29.66/24.45, while corresponding 3D-GS scores change from 28.69/23.14 to 28.88/23.60 (v1 Table 1; v3 Table 2). v3 adds results for two integrations, speed/storage measurements and diagnostic findings, while removing discarded ablation results. These are revised reported outcomes, not established same-setting version gains.

T1.justification: v1's normal-only error-function projection is replaced by a conditional-mean/variance formulation (v1 Equations 7 and 9; v3 Equations 8–11). v3 Appendix A.1 supplies a covariance-based derivation, and Appendix A.2 adds a Fourier-transform derivation for the one-dimensional Half-Gaussian. These materially expand and revise the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The central plug-and-play kernel, state-of-the-art rendering and preserved-speed claims remain. However, v3 drops the introduction's specific claim that the learned splitting-plane normal provides a solution for learning better surface normals, focusing its contribution statements on novel-view synthesis.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting Half-Gaussian frequency content to reduced Gibbs oscillations and opacity asymmetry to efficient tile selection. It removes v1's explicit qualification that improvements are weaker in featureless regions and its limitation concerning geometry reconstruction there. Interpretations of learning-rate instability and fine-tuning effectiveness also disappear with their studies.

D1.justification: v3 adds bounding-ellipse pseudocode, a normal/opacity learning-rate decay schedule, integration-specific settings and a project link advertised as providing code and demos. It removes several explicit v1 Appendix A.1 details, including 30,000-iteration budgets, densification/reset timing, Scaffold architecture settings, loss weights and CPU information. The RTX 3090 disclosure remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds FlashGS, GS-MCMC and SAGS, including FlashGS as inspiration for efficient bounds, and removes the PEFT survey associated with the discarded fine-tuning study. Its positioning relative to the closest kernel-changing methods, 2D-GS and GES, remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: the method description is separated into kernel, rasterization and splatting subsections; retained kernel-ablation material is redistributed into setup and results; and the appendix becomes separate derivation, implementation and results sections. The introduction, results discussion and conclusion are extensively revised around the new explanatory and efficiency evidence.

P2.justification: v3 switches to a two-column layout and substantially rearranges the displays. Existing kernel/pipeline diagrams are split and recombined, the qualitative montage is condensed, and appendix tables are merged and transposed. New fitting, frequency, speed, opacity and bounding-region figures replace the dataset overview and learning-rate plot; the main comparison table gains paired method groups and annotated PSNR differences.

improvement.justification: The covariance-aware derivation and direct speed/storage comparisons better substantiate the central method and efficiency claims, which v1 supported less fully. The net gain is limited by removing useful ablations, reproducibility settings and the featureless-region limitation. Numerical reporting also remains problematic: v3 Table 5 reports HGS-MCMC Tanks&Temples SSIM as 0.841 although its two scene values are 0.841 and 0.902.
